No.24

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Says: You Do Not Lack Good Roots — You Are Only Defeated by This One Thing

Amid phones, the internet and floods of information, finding focus and reflection again.

Author's record · translated; the Chinese original is authoritative

Open in reading mode →

🔶Inquiry to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

I asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva about "information anxiety" and "focus in practice".

People today are bombarded with fragmented information from phones, the internet and social media, so that their attention has seriously declined and their minds are scattered, making it hard to keep making progress.

This directly blocks deepening in "hearing, reflecting and practicing". Please tell us your thoughts.

🔶The Bodhisattva's Teaching

"Thoughts arise like lightning; the mind chases dust and flies. The web is like an ocean, its shimmering waves of ten thousand images confuse the eyes and disturb the heart. Beings chase information as ants chase sugar, gaining a moment's knowledge and losing lasting wisdom. Hearing much without reflecting, reflecting much without practicing — thus knowledge overflows while wisdom withers. Practitioners today do not lack good roots; they are defeated by distraction, lost in impermanent sounds and sights.

If you wish to return to the true, you must stop the empty rushing; gather the mind into one, and listen to the mind in stillness. If you can be still five minutes a day, the seed of concentration first sprouts; if one thought can dwell on a single line of a sutra, the root of wisdom grows again. If the mind is like a torch, ten thousand messages are stilled of themselves; if the mind is like dust, any wind scatters it.

Therefore the practitioner should make the mind the master and the device the servant, and not turn the servant into the master, losing one's own way.

🔶Plain Rendering

"Thoughts arise like lightning; the mind chases dust and flies." A thought arises as fast as lightning, and the mind runs everywhere after the noise of the world. "The web is like an ocean, its shimmering waves confuse the eyes and disturb the heart." The internet is like a vast sea of endless light and change, dazzling the eyes and scattering the mind. "Beings chase information as ants chase sugar, gaining a moment's knowledge and losing lasting wisdom."

People today chase information like ants running after sugar: they gain a moment of something new, but lose deep and lasting wisdom.

"Hearing much without reflecting, reflecting much without practicing — thus knowledge overflows while wisdom withers."

We hear a great deal but do not think it through; we think a great deal but do not practice; so knowledge piles up while wisdom dries out.

"Practitioners today do not lack good roots; they are defeated by distraction."

Practitioners today are not without good roots; they are defeated by a scattered mind, lost in ever-changing stimulation of sound and light.

"To return to the true, stop the empty rushing; gather the mind into one, listen to the mind in stillness."

If you want to return to a true and clear state, you must stop pointless chasing; bring the mind back and let it rest in stillness.

"Five minutes of stillness a day, and the seed of concentration sprouts; one thought on a single line of a sutra, and the root of wisdom grows again."

If you can be quiet for five minutes each day, the seed of meditation begins to sprout; if you can rest a single focused thought on one sutra, on one line of scripture, the root of wisdom grows again.

"If the mind is like a torch, ten thousand messages go out; if the mind is like dust, any wind scatters it."

If the mind is steady and bright like a torch, even endless information will naturally settle; if the mind is light as dust, any passing wind will throw it into disorder.

"Make the mind the master and the device the servant; do not let the servant become the master."

So practitioners should let the mind be the master and phones and the internet be the servants, and never let the tools take control and make you lose your own direction.
